article_text:
Listen to Ibrahim Mahama speak, and he’s likely to credit his success to his community, which includes market women, weavers, craftsmen, studio assistants, railway workers, curators, professors, and fellow artists.

The Ghanaian artist is quick to recognize their contributions when he receives one of the many awards he’s picked up recently. Ranked at the top of the influential ArtReview Power 100 list in 2025, he also won an Art Basel Gold Award that year and received the 2026 Arnold Bode prize. He was also recently named a chevalier of the French government’s Ordre des Arts et des Lettres; the honor was bestowed upon him in Ghana by Diarra Dime Labille, France’s Ambassador to the West African country.

“We live and work in a community and nobody is an island by themselves. I built my practice based on the idea of collectivity and working with different collaborators,” Mahama explained in an interview with ARTnews . As an example, he cited the scornful and at times suspicious reactions of Mallam Atta market women in Accra when he started collecting worn-out jute sacks at the early stage of his career, especially because he was still in college when he began producing those works. (The works he produced using those sacks quickly gained him fame, with some memorably appearing in Okwui Enwezor’s Venice Biennale in 2015.) As he spent time with the market women, they came to understand what he was doing and continued supporting him, helping him collect the sacks that still recur in his art.

“I think the artist is just a vessel, and I see myself as that vessel in order to put all these different things together to do the work that we do,” he added.

Mahama has become one of the most internationally visible Ghanaian artists, showing his work at biennials and museums across the world, and directing his success back to Ghana: The money from the sales of Mahama’s work is directed toward building institutions that he founds, including the Tamale-based Red Clay Studio and the Savannah Centre for Contemporary Art. He’s also bought dilapidated or abandoned buildings, factories, and airplanes, and turned them into art and educational spaces, as he did with Nkrumah Voli-ni, also in Tamale.

These projects, which Mahama called a “lifetime work,” breathe new life into collected materials, archives, industrial and national heritage. His work at times extends beyond Ghana to include international like with people like the Kenyan British artist Michael Armitage and his Nairobi Contemporary Art Institute. Learning from those conversations and becoming part of a large community expands the scope of what is possible is Mahama’s practice.

On Thursday, Mahama will open yet another epic project: “The Harvest Season,” an exhibition at the Fondation Cartier pour l’art contemporain in Paris, whose entire building he will take over starting next week. The show is “the most ambitious exhibition I’ve done,” Mahama said.

Parliament of Ghosts , an ongoing installation made of discarded train seats, railway sleepers, school furniture, worn-out jute sacks, and government archives that premiered in 2019 will figure in the Fondation Cartier show in a new iteration that adds about 200 collected and restored royal stools from the Asante Empire.

The idea, Mahama said, is to highlight a contradiction: These same stools, which are often looted before being exhibited in Western museums, are at times placed in glass cases. At the Fondation Cartier, people will have free access to them. He hopes this will invert questions around the return of African objects from Europe, asking: What happens when these stools are brought from Ghana to Europe as “living” objects and utilized for their original purpose, and not in museum cases or glasses? Doing so brings out the “the ghosts [and] histories” of these stools, creating an avenue for different conversations, he added.

There’s also a new project created by Mahama for this exhibition centered on the Aboso Glass Factory, which was established in 1966 by Ghana’s first president, Kwame Nkrumah, as part of the country’s industrialization efforts, before he was overthrown in a coup in that same year. Titled Things Fall Apart, after the 1958 novel by Nigerian author Chinua Achebe, it is a reconstruction of the abandoned glass bottle manufacturing plant that Mahama purchased some two years ago with production funds from Fondation Cartier.

The Paris installation is only a small part of the project, however, since the glass factory is being rebuilt in spaces including Red Clay Studio in Tamale and a British-era colonial building. When the Fondation Cartier exhibition ends, the factory will be returned to Ghana for permanent installation in Kumasi, where Mahama plans to build a new institution. He is also working with cinema owners and local craftsmen to explore the possibility of rebuilding some abandoned cinemas in the country.

In addition, a collection of works on the Ghanaian railway system will also be on display in the exhibition. A new textile installation using Ghanaian fabrics produced in northern Ghana, truck inner tubes, jute sacks, and found textiles will be hung across the arcades on the facades of the Fondation Cartier building.

“There is a dialogue between this old building [constructed in the 1850s] and Ibrahim’s work, which addresses the history of the 19th century in Ghana, and the links between what was happening between Europe and West Africa at that time,” said Aby Gaye-Duparc, the curator of the exhibition.

“What we really want to convey to the audience is that there are two sides of [Mahama]’s artistic practice,” said Gaye-Duparc. “There’s work that we see: installations, videos, work on paper. Everything comes from this community in Tamale that he has built because a lot of the installations were made first in Tamale and then travel to Paris or other venues.”

The other part, Gaye-Duparc continued, “is the work behind it that is being built in Tamale,” referring to the artist’s building of artistic infrastructure and institutions in the Northern Ghana city. These structures, she added, have expanded access to the arts for people who were left out for various reasons.

In line with Mahama’s collaborative approach, the Paris exhibition will also feature work by artists and collectives including James Barnor, Gideon Appah, CATPC (Cercle d’Art des Travailleurs de Plantation Congolaise), Tjaša Rener, Postbox Ghana, Courage Dzidula Kpodo, and Dorothy Akpene Amenuke, Mahama’s mentor.

Kpodo, an architect, will exhibit work that addresses modernism, turning the focus away from tropical modernism centered on concrete buildings, which were often built by foreigners in Ghanaian cities. The central piece will be a wall reconstruction made out of laterite from a building he owns in Gyampo, in the Eastern Region, used in so-called vernacular or traditional buildings. The installation will include about 100 postcards by the Postbox Ghana collective depicting tropical modernist architectural buildings in cities such as Accra, Kumasi and Takoradi.

“I would describe Ibrahim as someone who makes space within his own abilities and means for people that he thinks are doing interesting, important work,” said Kpodo.

The Fondation Cartier exhibition is one of the first major ones by Mahama staged since he was viciously attacked earlier this year by a special operations unit of the Ghana Police Service in Tamale, where he lives and works. Mahama noted the community support that he received during the fallout, saying, “It was fantastic, I must say. I was really overwhelmed, because sometimes you don’t realize how much your work means to people.” He added that people traveled from within Tamale and from other cities like Accra and Kumasi came to visit him, express regret, and bemoan the treatment meted out to him by the police, especially because of his considerable contributions to the city.

He said he was unaware of the current state of the investigations into the matter by the Criminal Investigation Department as directed by Ghana’s Inspector General of Police because he hadn’t received updates in months. But he also seemed more interested in concentrating on his art. “I want to channel my energy into this positive part of my practice of what I do and what it means to the community,” he explained. “But certainly, I am also quite disappointed in the way that it was handled by the police. And I hope that at some point, we will be able to at least know more [about the investigations], so that we see what direction to take it in.” He plans to follow up again when he settles back in Ghana by the end of the year from his travels.

For now, he is more focused on supporting the community he has helped create. “I’m happy that the work I do has a very profound meaning and effect on people who live on our continent, in particular Ghana. I am also interested in how this work is traveling around the world, stretching the African sensibilities, and what we are bringing to art in the 21st century.”

Cartelera de Cinépolis – Estrenos del 26 de noviembre, 2026

Staff Cine PREMIERE

¿Qué verás esta semana?

Esta semana la cartelera Cinépolis se renueva con una selección de estrenos que van desde grandes producciones comerciales hasta propuestas más arriesgadas para quienes buscan algo distinto en la sala de cine. Ya sea que tengas ganas de una historia emotiva, un thriller intenso o puro entretenimiento para desconectarte, los nuevos lanzamientos ofrecen opciones para todos los gustos. ¿Qué películas nuevas llegan a la cartelera de Cinépolis? Entérate aquí.

Aquí te contamos cuáles son las películas que llegan a la cartelera Cinépolis esta semana y la siguiente. Una guía rápida para decidir qué ver, cuándo ir y no perderte los títulos más comentados del momento.

Cartelera Cinépolis: estrenos del jueves 26 de noviembre de 2026

La nueva Focker (Focker-in-Law) / Dir. John Hamburg / EE. UU. / 2026

Hechizo: Bienvenidos a Hexe (Hexed) / Dirs. Jason Hand, Fawn Veerasunthorn, Josie Trinidad / EE. UU. / 2026 Una adolescente poco convencional descubre habilidades mágicas secretas que, una vez desatadas, la arrojan a un vasto reino de brujas llamado Hexe. Haciendo equipo con su madre, descubren misterios familiares que podrían cambiar el mundo de las brujas para siempre.

Me encontraste (L’âme idéale) / Dir.a Alice Vial / Francia / 2025 Elsa, de 40 años y soltera, ha abandonado la esperanza del amor. Su inusual don de ver y hablar con los muertos la aísla de los demás. Luego conoce a Oscar, un hombre encantador que reaviva su fe en las posibilidades.

Puedes verlo todo (You Can See Everything) – Documental / Dir. Nathan Fielder, Lance Oppenheim / EE. UU. / 2026 Treinta y cuatro días antes de ser enviada a prisión, la famosa fundadora de Theranos, Elizabeth Holmes, invita a un equipo de filmación escéptico a documentar cada uno de sus movimientos. Lo que comienza como un retrato íntimo se convierte en un alucinante viaje de tres años.

La nueva Focker (Focker-in-Law) / Dir. John Hamburg / EE. UU. / 2026 Un joven llamado Henry, hijo de Greg y Pam Focker, se enfrenta al caos familiar cuando decide casarse con una mujer de carácter fuerte que parece no ser compatible con él. Protagonizan Roberto De Niro, Ben Stiller, Teri Polo y Ariana Grande.

El diablo sabe tu nombre / Dir. Andres Beltran / México / 2026 Unos cineastas que investigan el incendio de una residencia de ancianos en el que murieron varios niños descubren el impactante acto de una joven voluntaria y a una exorcista del Vaticano que insiste en que su crimen se debió a una posesión demoníaca.

Doce lunas / Dir.a Victoria Franco / México / 2026 Sofía, una arquitecta de 40 años de la Ciudad de México, lidia con la pérdida personal, los problemas de fertilidad y su identidad mientras su vida se desmorona, lo que la obliga a buscar fuerza interior y autodescubrimiento.

También te podría interesar: Cartelera de Cinépolis – Estrenos de esta semana .

Mi amigo el sol / Dir.a Alejandra Patrica Pérez González / México / 2026

Digger / Dir. Alejandro González Iñárritu / EE. UU. / 2026

¿Qué llegará la próxima semana a la cartelera Cinépolis (jueves 3 de diciembre 2026)?

¡Behemoth! (Behemoth!) / Dir. Tony Gilroy / EE. UU. / 2026

Hombres íntegros / Dir. Alejandro Andrade / México, España, Francia / 2026 Cuando Alf regresa a la escuela tras un año de ausencia, comienza a entablar amistad con Oliver, un nuevo alumno. Esto dañará profundamente la relación entre Alf y Oliver, ya que Alf se enfrenta solo a la transición a la adultez, envuelto en el mundo del crimen.

La psicópata (Victorian Psycho) / Dir. Zachary Wigon / Reino Unido, Irlanda, EE. UU. / 2026 En 1858, una joven y excéntrica institutriz, Winifred Notty, llega a la remota mansión gótica de Ensor House. A medida que Winifred se adapta, el personal comienza a desaparecer inexplicablemente, y los propietarios se preguntan si algo anda mal con esta nueva institutriz.

Otra mujer sin filtro / Dir.a Gabriela Sobarzo / Chile / 2026 La historia sigue a Luisa (Tato Alexander), una activista radical que, tras ser atropellada durante una protesta, cambia por completo hacia una postura ultraconservadora y dice todo sin filtro, poniendo a prueba su relación con su pareja, Ricardo (Ricardo O’Farrill).

Gohan / Dirs. Chayanop Boonprakob, Atta Hemwadee, Baz Poonpiriya / Tailandia / 2026 La historia narra los vínculos entre humanos y animales siguiendo a un perro callejero llamado Gohan a lo largo de una década, mientras vive con dueños temporales, en buenos y malos momentos, en alegrías y tristezas, en saludos y despedidas.

¡Behemoth! (Behemoth!) / Dir. Tony Gilroy / EE. UU. / 2026 Narra la historia de un músico proveniente de una familia de músicos que regresa a Los Ángeles. Una carta de amor a la música del cine y a quienes la crean. Protagonizan Pedro Pascal y Olivia Wilde.

Diplo en el reino de los dibujos perdidos / Dir. Wojtek Wawszczyk / República Checa, EE. UU, Polonia, Eslovaquia / 2024 Cuando el mundo que le rodea desaparece misteriosamente, un pequeño dinosaurio verde viaja a través de las páginas de un cómic para devolverle el color a su hogar.

Fragmentos del olvido / Dir. Rubén Villa / México / 2024 David, un terapeuta de éxito, es el creador de un método nunca antes utilizado en la psicología moderna: un dispositivo que le permite alterar los recuerdos más dolorosos de sus pacientes.

article_text:
Sergei Loznitsa’s “Imperium,” which revisits the Soviet Union of the early 1970s through footage shot by Italian cameramen, has won the best film award at the 70th BFI London Film Festival competition.

The prizes were unveiled Sunday as the festival drew to a close. The competition jury was led by filmmaker Sam Pollard, whose credits include “MLK/FBI” and “Citizen Ashe,” and also featured “Life of Jorge Luis Borges” filmmaker Mariano Llinás and DDA chief strategy officer Julie La Bassiere.

Related Stories

Egyptian Cinema Eyes Its Next Act as Industry Veterans Call for Better Scripts, Wider Distribution

“The film is richly evocative and emotionally engaging on all levels giving us a visually arresting perspective of life before the Soviet Union was broken apart,” the jury said.

Popular on Variety

In the first feature competition, the Sutherland Award went to Thailand’s Oscar submission “9 Temples to Heaven,” the first fiction feature from Sompot Chidgasornpongse. The film reflects on faith, kinship and the passage from life to death. Actor Amir El-Masry (“Giant,” “Limbo”) presided over that jury, joined by “Moonglow” producer Alemberg Ang and sales, distribution and awards strategist Rosa Bosch.

“An accomplished first feature paving his own path in the well-established tradition of filmmaking in the Southeast Asian region,” the jury said.

Bertil Nilsson’s “Masc” received a special mention in the same section. The debut tracks Robin, who drifts between short-term jobs and uncertain relationships while looking for somewhere he fits. The jury singled out Nilsson as a fresh British talent with an unusual concept and a funny script.

The Grierson Award for documentary went to Asmahan Bkerat’s feature directorial debut “Concrete Land,” which spends time with several generations of a mixed-race family in Jordan as they resist displacement and hostility. “Santosh” director Sandhya Suri headed the documentary jury, alongside Melbourne International Film Festival senior programmer Kate Fitzpatrick and BAFTA and Emmy-winning producer Andee Ryder.

“In a noisy and often polemical world it was refreshing, humbling and deeply relevant to see the quiet resilience and dignity of this family in the face of the erasure of their culture and traditions,” the jury said.

Theo Rollason’s “Queer Edward II,” assembled entirely from archive material, earned a special mention. It goes behind the scenes of Derek Jarman’s “Edward II,” set against the anti-LGBTQIA+ laws Britain passed in the 1980s, and the jury praised it as a portrait of Jarman the artist and Jarman the activist.

Rahul Roye’s “Aman” won the Short Film Award. The film centers on a trans man who learns he is pregnant the night before his gender-affirming surgery, upending his sense of who he is as a man and as a father. It is streaming free on BFI Player until Oct. 25.

Writer-producer Helen Simmons (“100 Nights of Hero”) led the shorts jury, which also included comedian Leo Reich and script editor Jack Casey.

“We were struck by the film’s painterly cinematography, and expansive and assured storytelling, which guided us through the world with care,” the jury said.

Elizabeth Hobbs’ “Daughters of the Late Colonel,” about two middle-aged sisters left adrift after the death of their domineering father, took a special mention for its inventive visual style.

Audience voting for the festival’s best feature film and best British discovery prizes closes Oct. 21, with winners to be named later. Last year, Chloé Zhao’s “Hamnet” took the audience prize for best feature, while Yemi Bamiro’s “Black Is Beautiful: The Kwame Brathwaite Story” won British discovery.

article_text:
Oscar-winning French actor Marion Cotillard will preside over the competition jury at the 23rd Marrakech Film Festival in November.

Alongside her to be announced jury members, the “Inception” and “Dark Knight Rises” star will lead the decision of which film is awarded the Étoile d’Or out of Marrakech’s international competition, which consists of first and second features.

“I have been fortunate enough to attend the Marrakech International Film Festival since its very beginnings; I’ve had wonderful experiences there and met some truly remarkable people,” Cotillard said in a statement. “Supporting filmmakers as they take their first steps is a vital part of what this festival is all about — it’s in its DNA — and it is a great joy for me to chair the jury this year.”

Related Stories

'La Bola Negra' to Receive Gotham Vanguard Tribute at Gotham Film Awards (EXCLUSIVE)

Queer Bodybuilder Drama 'Test' Acquired by Dark Star Pictures (EXCLUSIVE)

Cotillard first broke out in the 1998 French action comedy “Taxi,” before making her Hollywood debut in Tim Burton’s “Big Fish” in 2003. In 2007, she portrayed French singer Édith Piaf in “La Vie en Rose” and won the Oscar for best actress, becoming the first actor to win an Academy Award for a French-language performance. She earned her second best actress Oscar nomination in 2015 for the Dardenne Brothers’ drama “Two Days, One Night.”

Most recently, she starred in Guillaume Canet’s Cannes-premiering “Karma,” “Lee” alongside Kate Winslet and on the TV series “The Morning Show” opposite Jennifer Aniston and Reese Witherspoon. She is currently filming “The Enraged,” a historical drama from Emmanuelle Bercot.

This year’s Marrakech Film Festival takes place from Nov. 20-28.

article_text:
Netflix has bought a raft of films and series from Brazilian powerhouse Globo including Walter Salles ’ Oscar-winning movie I’m Still Here .

The U.S. streamer’s agreement with Globo fare is the largest ever programming deal between the two. Netflix has acquired a package of fourteen movies, a trio of telenovelas and a TV series.

The deal for I’m Still Here is just for Brazil . Elsewhere, Netflix has taken global rights to titles including Vitória , directed by Andrucha Waddington and starring the Academy Award nominee Fernanda Montenegro.

Related Stories

Ju Ji-hoon & Choo Young-woo Return To 'The Trauma Code: Heroes On Call' With Seasons 2 & 3 In Production At Netflix

Curtain Up: 'La Bola Negra' Shines As Netflix Shares Grosses In Historic First -- Specialty Box Office

Another Brazil-only rights deal is for comedy series Vai Que Cola , created by Leandro Soares and directed by João Fonseca and Regis Faria. Netflix has acquired seven seasons of the show.

Watch on Deadline

The telenovela selection includes India – A Love Story . Created by Glória Perez and directed by Marcos Schechtman, it won the 2009 International Emmy for Best Telenovela. Specifically, Netflix has it for the U.S. and Latin America.

The titles will drop on Netflix from mid-2027.

“For decades, we have been dedicated to sharing the richness of our culture with the world,” said Pedro Garcia, Globo’s Director of Rights. “By combining that experience with Netflix’s global scale, we take another step toward bringing Brazilian creativity to new audiences, expanding the presence and strengthening the recognition of Brazilian film and television abroad.”

The agreement is a big sales story for Globo. Meanwhile, the Brazilian media giant has also been in buying mode. It has acquired game show The Perfect Line from Paramount Global Content Distribution.

The series bowed on GSN in the U.S. In Brazil, the local version will feature as a segment on Globo’s Saturday afternoon entertainment show Caldeirão com Mion .

article_text:
Founded in 2018 in partnership with the French Ministry of Culture, the Elles × Paris Photo program highlights the work of women artists and their role in the history and current landscape of photography and images. The program has helped raise the representation of women artists at the fair from 20% to 38%.

For this new edition, Paris Photo has entrusted the curation of the program to Aldeide Delgado. On the occasion of the Bicentennial of Photography, she presents An Oceanic Beginning , a selection that returns to the material conditions at the origin of the photographic image and takes the ocean as a framework for reflection. By putting historical and contemporary practices in dialogue, the program envisions a history of photography without a fixed center, made up of interconnected narratives, some of which are handed down while others remain invisible.

“On the occasion of the Bicentennial of Photography, An Oceanic Beginning looks at the resources and conditions necessary for the creation of photographs. The sea becomes the starting point for a reflection on how the history of photography can be told.” — Aldeide Delgado

Marked on the map handed out at the entrance and also available online and in a dedicated publication, the program offers a guiding thread for exploring the fair. It continues throughout the year with a series of video and written interviews, shared on the Paris Photo website, social media and YouTube channel.

About the Curator

Aldeide Delgado is an art historian, curator and founder of WOPHA (Women Photographers International Archive), an institution dedicated to promoting women and non-binary artists in the history of photography.

Her research draws in particular on feminist and decolonial approaches to broaden the narratives of the history of photography.

Daily Newsletter

The “Renegade Housewife” of Pop Art

Stories from a pioneering journalist and art worker, John Yau on Valerio Adami, and books of warp and weft for your reading list.

At age 98, Joan Kron has lived many lives. She invented plastic surgery journalism, helped Andy Warhol make his first perfume, hosted the Velvet Underground’s first Philly concert, and commissioned Roy Lichtenstein’s “Super Sunset Billboard.”

That 1967 artwork, a remake of which is on view in the late Pop artist’s exhibition at the Whitney, is one of countless projects she has wrangled into being from behind the scenes. In an exclusive interview today, the indefatigable Kron regales reporter Isabella Segalovich with a slice of those riotous stories, with more to come in her memoir titled The Renegade Housewives of Pop Art — I’ll be first in line at the bookstore.

Also today: WPA-era murals by Black artists in Harlem are finally restored, the art world descends on a champagne-soaked Frieze London, we recommend books on the rich histories of textile art, and critic John Yau finds echoes of Pop art in the paintings of Valerio Adami.

—Lakshmi Rivera Amin, associate editor

Danh Vo and Sandra Mujinga are selected for Met Museum commissions, a new leader is named for the Armenian Museum of America, Bernie Sanders weighs in on the AI art debate, and more in Art Movements .

article_text:
MoN Takanawa: The Museum of Narratives は、英国を代表する総合文化施設Barbican Centre（バービカン・センター）との共同制作による没入型サウンドエキシビション 「Feel the Sound（フィール・ザ・サウンド）」 を開催する。本展は、音や振動、音楽、テクノロジーが融合したインスタレーションを通して、音を身体全体で感じる展覧会だ。日本では初めての開催となり、バービカン・センターで初公開された作品群に加え、既存作を再構成した作品、東京開催に合わせた新作3点が公開される。会期は11月20日から2027年3月22日まで。

本展の見どころは、国内外のアーティストによる作品群だ。それぞれの作家が独自の視点で「音」を解釈し、来場者の感覚や身体を揺さぶる。 坂本龍一 と 真鍋大度 によるコラボレーション作品《Sensing Streams》は、現代社会に不可欠なテクノロジーが発する電磁波に着目したインスタレーション。周囲の環境から取得したデータを音と光に変換し、普段は知覚できない情報の流れを体感できる。

マックス・クーパー の《Reflections of Being》は、「日常生活では表現できないと感じていることは何ですか？」という問いに寄せられた匿名の声をもとに、音楽・映像・テキストで構成された没入型インスタレーション。他者の思考や感情にふれられる。

インド各地の音楽文化や工芸、職人の技、デジタルテクノロジーを組み合わせたElsewhere in Indiaのインスタレーション《Resonance Continuum》では、来場者が実際に身体を使って音を体験できる。

これらの作品を含め、本展は全12の空間で構成される。キュレーター、 ルーク・ケンプ は次のようにコメントしている。 「来場者は、12の個性豊かな空間を通して、音を聴覚だけでとらえるものではなく、見て、感じて、触れられるものとして探求できます。新たな展開を加えた本展を東京で初めて紹介し、皆さまに体験していただけることを、大変楽しみにしています」 。英国と日本の共同制作が生み出す、音の新体験に注目したい。

title_original: Reimagining Liberation: Brandon Gercara Between Maloya and Voguing
editorial_title_zh: 重新想象解放：Brandon Gercara 如何让 Maloya 与 Voguing 相遇
editorial_excerpt_zh: 留尼汪艺术家 Brandon Gercara 在法国诺瓦谢尔的 La Ferme du Buisson 展出《Destin Vogoya》。展览将当地的 Maloya 音乐传统与 Voguing 舞结合，通过表演、摄影等媒介探讨酷儿身份、文化记忆与解放的可能。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "在法国诺瓦谢尔的 La Ferme du Buisson 艺术中心，留尼汪艺术家 Brandon Gercara 的展览《Destin Vogoya》通过表演、视觉艺术和想象性叙事，让酷儿表达、去殖民思想与文化传统展开对话。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/still-2026-03-17-173703_1-107-2-1030x579.webp", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "传承下来的传统，如何成为争取解放的工具？在《Destin Vogoya》中，留尼汪艺术家 Brandon Gercara 探索酷儿身份、文化记忆与抵抗之间的交汇，以艺术实验挑战既有的权力结构。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这是 Gercara 首次在当代艺术中心举办个展。展览呈现虚构世界 Majik Kwir 的新篇章，故事围绕来自留尼汪的七位 LGBTQIA+ 主角展开。展览的核心是 vogoya：一种将 Maloya 与 Voguing 融合的形式。前者是一种根植于留尼汪抵抗历史的音乐传统，后者则是与黑人及拉美裔酷儿舞厅文化密切相关的舞蹈。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Gercara 的创作横跨表演、摄影、录像、装置、素描与绘画，探究文化实践如何通过重新诠释，为不同的身份认同和集体表达开辟空间。这种跨媒介的创作方式借鉴去殖民女性主义、交叉性和克里奥尔化思想，把艺术实践视为质疑主流社会叙事的途径。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览之外，Gercara 也通过支持留尼汪 LGBTQIA+ 社群的 Requeer 项目开展社会行动，推动社群获得更多公共可见性，并促进文化交流。《Destin Vogoya》邀请观众思考：传统、想象力与集体创造，如何为归属感和解放带来新的可能。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览在法国诺瓦谢尔的 La Ferme du Buisson 举行，展期至2027年1月24日。", "links": [{"text": "La Ferme du Buisson", "url": "https://www.lafermedubuisson.com/fr/brandon-gercara"}], "translated": true}]

article_text:
At La Ferme du Buisson in Noisiel, France, Réunionese artist Brandon Gercara’s ‘Destin Vogoya’ brings queer expression, decolonial thought and cultural traditions into dialogue through performance, visual art and speculative storytelling.

How can inherited traditions become instruments of liberation? In ‘Destin Vogoya’, Réunionese artist Brandon Gercara explores the intersections of queer identity, cultural memory and resistance, challenging established structures of power through artistic experimentation.

Marking Gercara’s first solo exhibition at a contemporary art centre, the presentation introduces a new chapter of Majik Kwir , a fictional universe following seven LGBTQIA+ protagonists from Réunion. Central to the exhibition is vogoya, a hybrid form bringing together maloya, a musical tradition rooted in Réunion’s history of resistance, and voguing, a dance form associated with Black and Latin American queer ballroom culture.

Working across performance, photography, video, installation, drawing and painting, Gercara examines how cultural practices can be reinterpreted to create spaces for alternative identities and collective expression. Their multidisciplinary approach draws on decolonial feminism, intersectionality and creolisation, positioning artistic practice as a means of questioning dominant social narratives.

Beyond the exhibition, Gercara’s activism through Requeer, an initiative supporting LGBTQIA+ communities in Réunion, reflects their commitment to visibility and cultural exchange. ‘Destin Vogoya’ invites audiences to consider how tradition, imagination and collective creativity can generate new possibilities for belonging and emancipation.

This exhibition is on view at La Ferme du Buisson , Noisiel, France, until 24 January 2027.

article_text:
Morgan Neville has made documentaries about some of the most influential cultural figures in recent history, from Brian Wilson and Keith Richards to Fred Rogers and Lorne Michaels . But there’s no challenge quite like a Beatle.

His latest film , “Man on the Run,” focuses on Paul McCartney ‘s decade following the end of The Beatles. The documentary captures his move to rural Scotland, the formation of his second major band Wings, and the recording of seminal albums like “McCartney” and “Ram.” It captures McCartney’s solo career with the same gravitas as Peter Jackson’s “Get Back,” shining light on an era of music that is often dismissed when compared to his earlier masterpieces.

At IndieWire’s Art of the Doc event on Monday, October 19, Neville sat down with IndieWire editor-in-chief Brent Lang to discuss bringing the Beatle’s story to the big screen. He explained that, despite there being so many recent documentaries about The Beatles, McCartney’s Wings era offered an untold story that could shine new light on one of the greatest songwriters of all time.

“I got a call, I met with him, and I told him this film ends the day The Beatles broke up and it ends the day John Lennon dies,” Neville said of the project’s origins.

The director went on to explain that the McCartney we see for much of the film was scarred by the aftermath of his early fame and the acrimonious breakup of his band. His retreat to pastoral family life was a necessary step in reconnecting with his own musical talents.

“There was some PTSD that all of them had from going through being a Beatle. They just didn’t ever have to grow up … in certain ways they never had to deal with reality,” he said. “People were angry, and that trauma turned into anger, like ‘Why can’t you guys just get back together?’ and blaming everybody. Linda’s idea was to go off to this tiny farmhouse to the middle of nowhere in Scotland. Which sounded a little insane, but probably was the sanest decision they ever made.”

Watch the complete conversation with Neville in the video above.

National Geographic Documentary Films, part of a joint venture between The Walt Disney Company and the National Geographic Society, is committed to bringing the world premium, feature documentaries that cover timely, provocative and globally relevant stories from the very best documentary filmmakers. Its award-winning and critically acclaimed films reach 300 million people worldwide in 180 countries and 33 languages across the global National Geographic channels and direct-to-consumer platforms Disney+ and Hulu.

Recent films include the Emmy-nominated winner of the IDA Award for Best Feature “The Tale of Silyan;” Oscar® and Peabody nominee “Sugarcane;” Oscar-nominated and Peabody Award winner “Bobi Wine: The People’s President;” Emmy Award winner “Lost In The Jungle;” Oscar- and BAFTA-nominated “Fire of Love;” Emmy and Peabody Award winner “The Territory;” BAFTA nominees “The Rescue” and “Becoming Cousteau;” and Oscar- and BAFTA winner “Free Solo.” For more information visit films.nationalgeographic.com , or find us on Facebook , Twitter , Instagram , and YouTube .

写真家・中島大輔が、18年ぶりとなる写真集『some, same それぞれ、おなじ』を2026年11月22日（日）に刊行する。20日（金）までプレオーダーを受け付けている。また、これを記念した個展「some, same」が、12月4日（金）から20日（日）まで、東京・六本木のPost-Fakeで開催される。

1983年大阪生まれの中島は、2007年にキヤノン写真新世紀準グランプリを受賞。翌2008年に写真集『each other』（青幻舎）を発表して以来、身体やセクシュアリティを題材とした作品を制作してきた。

新作『some, same』では、SNSを通じて声をかけた男性たちの身体を撮影。インターネット上に公開された写真や動画、テキストの断片を手がかりに被写体と向き合い、フレーミングやアングル、クローズアップによって個人の背景や来歴を画面から取り除いていく。

「他者は、写っていない部分を無意識に補完する」と語る中島。写真に写された身体の断片を通して、見る側が何を想像し、何を読み取ろうとするのか。写真が現実を完全には捉えられないという性質から、視覚と認識の関係を問い直す。

写真集には、美術評論家・清水穣による同等性と愛をめぐる論考を収録。アートディレクションとデザインは坂脇慶が担当した。208ページ、布クロス装のハードカバーで、函入りの仕様。セルフパブリッシングによる500部限定で刊行される。9900円（六切プリント付き限定版55000円、全40セット）。

個展では、写真集に収録された作品から発色現像方式によるプリント10点を展示し、会場で写真集も販売する。

タイトル

中島大輔 個展「some, same」

場所

Post-Fake（東京都港区六本木5-2-4 3F）

会期

2026年12月4日（金）〜20日（日）

時間

14:00〜19:00（土・日曜日は12:00から）

休み

月～木曜日

URL

https://www.daisukenakashima.com/somesame

article_text:
“Obsession” star Inde Navarrette had quite the busy weekend, going from the Academy Museum Gala on Saturday to the Newport Beach Film Festival on Sunday.

Navarrette attended the festival, which runs until Thursday in Newport Beach, as one of Variety ’s 10 Actors to Watch, who were celebrated during the festival’s Honor Brunch.

While speaking with Variety’s Marc Malkin at the festival’s carpet, Navarrette said attending the gala was “amazing.” “I mean, you’re just overwhelmed and kind of drowning in everybody that you have looked up to, possibly ever, and it’s just so lovely meeting people and the reception that ‘Obsession’ has been getting… I’m just so honored to go and be with the members of the Academy and just get an inside scoop on what that magnificent world is like.”

Popular on Variety

Related Stories

'The Pitt' And 'All Her Fault' Among the Winners of Inaugural Easterseals Disability Arts & Culture Awards

Jessica Lange and Pamela Anderson were two of the actresses Navarrette was excited to see Saturday night. “I spoke to Jessica Lange, who is an icon,” she said. “[And] the way that Pamela carries herself with such grace and honesty and just pure creativity and love is just exactly who I want to be.”

And Navarrette’s schedule isn’t slowing down just yet — she’s set to host this year’s “Saturday Night Live” Halloween episode with musical guest Gracie Abrams.

“I literally I feel like I snuck in,” joked the actress. “I’m super excited to keep everything under wraps because I really truly want to make this super fun for the audience. And what I love is when I don’t know anything. So I’m really excited to be working with the writers.”

Also on the horizon is the MCU’s forthcoming “X-Men” film, in which she’ll play Rogue. Navarrette told Malkin she hasn’t corresponded directly with Anna Paquin, who originated the role, but feels “the correspondence started when I was younger, when I really fell in love with the ‘X-Men’ movies in the first place.”

On the topic of stunt training for the superhero film, Navarrette said it’s a good excuse to get herself in the gym. “I’ve always wanted to take part in that sort of a thing,” she said. “I think it’s also a really good excuse to get in the gym. I’m the laziest person, and I am very excited to get up and move my body.”

NOTICIAS

Elizabeth Olsen define a WandaVision como un «viaje salvaje»

Antonio G. Spíndola

Wanda Maximoff también acompañará próximamente al Hechicero Supremo en Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.

Entres las futuras series de Marvel que llegarán a la plataforma Disney+ se encuentran aquella que contará con el dúo Bruja Escarlata y Visión. El trágico romance del MCU podría aspirar a un alternativo e inexplicable final feliz, como anticipa el primer póster . No obstante, algo inquietante prevalece en aquella idílica imagen. No descartemos que WandaVision constituya (más bien) una aventura alocada, una posibilidad que recientemente señaló la actriz Elizabeth Olsen .

En entrevista para Entertainment Weekly , la intérprete de la poderosa mutante habló sobre las ansias que le genera explorar nuevas facetas de su personaje, con un mayor apego a las historietas.

«A partir de Era de Ultrón , las cosas que me encantaron de Scarlet Witch son cosas que vamos a explorar ahora. Estoy muy nerviosa y emocionada por eso en todas las formas divertidas. Pero creo que finalmente podremos recorrer algunos caminos de los cómics, que son favoritos, y explorar. Será un viaje salvaje ».

Durante la misma sesión de preguntas, el actor Paul Bettany (Visión) recalcó la oportunidad que les brinda la serie para profundizar en ambos personajes, y recalcó también la locura inherente a la propuesta narrativa.

«Creo que ha habido una auténtica progresión en los personajes, en la relación y en la posibilidad de ocupar el tiempo en eso. Cada vez hay cosas más emocionantes que podemos hacer. Los guiones que hasta ahora hemos leído son muy descabellados ».

En el reparto también se encuentran Kat Dennings (Darcy en Thor y Thor: Un mundo oscuro ) y Randall Park (Agent Woo en Ant-Man and the Wasp ), actores cómicos que seguramente harán honor a la definición de la serie como «mitad sitcom clásica, mitad espectáculo del MCU» .

WandaVision llegará a Disney+ en la primavera de 2021.

Antonio G. Spíndola Tengo muy mala memoria. Por solidaridad con mis recuerdos, opto por perderme también. De preferencia, en una sala de cine.
excerpt_original: Wanda Maximoff también acompañará próximamente al Hechicero Supremo en Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. La entrada Elizabeth Olsen define a WandaVision como un «viaje salvaje» se publicó primero en Cine PREMIERE .
